name: Reconsolidation and Retrieval-Mediated Learning
higher_order_principle: Memory retrieval temporarily destabilizes the retrieved trace, opening a reconsolidation window (~5-6 hours) during which the trace can be modified: strengthened by effortful retrieval, updated with new information (feedback), or weakened by interference. This is the mechanism underlying the testing effect: retrieval DESTABILIZES → restabilization STRENGTHENS. It also explains why immediate feedback after testing is more effective than delayed feedback — the reconsolidation window is open.
transferable_to: PTSD therapy (destabilize trauma memory → update with safety context)
skill refinement (reactivate motor program → correct error)
misconception correction (must activate wrong idea to fix it)

parameters.requirement: retrieval must ACTIVATE the trace (mere re-exposure may not trigger reconsolidation if the trace isn't fully reactivated)
parameters.protein_synthesis: restabilization requires protein synthesis, like initial consolidation

parameters.mechanism: Effortful retrieval (low RS, Bjork) may produce stronger reconsolidation because: (1) deeper trace reactivation, (2) more extensive PE signaling (the difficulty itself is a signal), (3) broader context encoding during the retrieval attempt.
parameters.easy_retrieval: minimal destabilization → minimal strengthening → minimal learning
parameters.failed_retrieval: trace not fully activated → reconsolidation may not trigger → but the ATTEMPT still generates PE that enhances subsequent encoding when the correct answer is provided (pretesting effect)

parameters.immediate_feedback: delivered within reconsolidation window → INTEGRATED into the destabilized trace → the error is corrected AT THE TRACE LEVEL, not just supplemented
parameters.delayed_feedback: delivered after window closes → creates a SEPARATE trace → both the error and the correction coexist as independent memories → less effective error correction

parameters.mechanism: Each retrieval creates a NEW hippocampal trace with the CURRENT temporal and spatial context. Multiple retrievals in different contexts → multiple traces with diverse context associations → more retrieval routes → more robust, more transferable memory.
parameters.connects_to_Bjork: Multiple traces = increased Storage Strength. Diverse contexts = increased accessibility across situations.

scope_conditions: Reconsolidation has boundary conditions: very strong, well-consolidated memories may resist destabilization (Dudai)
Reconsolidation requires trace REACTIVATION, not just cue presentation — the memory must be genuinely accessed
The 5-6 hour window is approximate and may vary with trace age and strength
Reconsolidation is demonstrated in fear memory (Nader) and increasingly in declarative memory, but the full educational application is still emerging
moderators: trace_age (older memories may be harder to destabilize)

interactions.description: Reconsolidation is often driven by prediction error (mismatch between retrieved memory and current reality). E6 describes the PE principle; E3 describes the trace mechanism.
Reconsolidation (E3) feeds back into Encoding (E1) — each retrieval is a new encoding event.

key_references: Nader, K., Schafe, G. E., & LeDoux, J. E. (2000). Fear memories require protein synthesis in the amygdala for reconsolidation. Nature
Dudai, Y. (2004). The neurobiology of consolidations. Annual Review of Psychology
Dudai, Y. (2006). Reconsolidation: The advantage of being refocused. Current Opinion in Neurobiology
